a01.question: Which statements are correct about an atom of ⁹⁹Tc (proton number 43)? (1) It has 13 more neutrons than protons. (2) It has 43 protons. (3) It has 99 nucleons.
a01.explanation: Neutrons = 99 − 43 = 56, which is 13 more than the 43 protons.

a01.question: Which statements are correct about an atom of ⁹⁹Tc (proton number 43)? (1) It has 13 fewer protons than neutrons. (2) It forms ⁹⁹Tc²⁺ which has 45 electrons. (3) It has 56 nucleons.
a01.explanation: Tc²⁺ has 41 electrons; 56 is the neutron number, the nucleon number is 99.

a01.question: The phosphide ion ³¹₁₅P³⁻ and the sulfide ion ³²₁₆S²⁻ have the same number of which particles? (1) neutrons (2) electrons (3) protons
a01.explanation: Both have 16 neutrons and 18 electrons; protons are 15 and 16.

a01.question: How many σ bonds are present in the molecule CH₂=CH–CH₂–C(=O)–O–CH₂–CH=CH₂?
a01.explanation: 10 C–H + 5 C–C + 1 C=O (σ part) + 2 C–O = 18.

a01.question: Radon (Z = 86), francium (Z = 87) and radium (Z = 88): what is the order of their first ionisation energies, least to most endothermic?
a01.explanation: Group 1 Fr is lowest, Group 2 Ra next, and the noble gas Rn is highest.

a01.question: In which species are the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons all different?
a01.explanation: ³⁹K⁺ has 19 p, 20 n, 18 e. The others each have two equal numbers.

a01.question: In which species are the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons all different?
a01.explanation: ²³Na⁺ has 11 p, 12 n, 10 e. F⁻ has n = e; P has p = e; S²⁻ has p = n.

a01.question: The first ionisation energies of twenty successive elements (letters not their real symbols) are shown. Which statements are correct? (1) Elements B, J and R are in Group 18. (2) Atoms of elements D and L contain two electrons in their outer shells. (3) Atoms of elements G and O contain a half-filled p subshell.
a01.explanation: B, J, R are He, Ne, Ar. D and L are Be and Mg. G and O are N and P (p^3).
a01.alt: Graph of first ionisation energy for 20 successive elements A to T, with peaks at B, J and R.

a01.question: Na(g) → Na⁺(g) + e⁻ ΔH = W; Na(g) → Na²⁺(g) + 2e⁻ ΔH = X; Na(s) → Na(g) ΔH = Y; Na(s) → Na²⁺(g) + 2e⁻ ΔH = Z. What is the second ionisation energy of sodium?
a01.explanation: Second IE = (loss of two electrons) − (loss of the first) = X − W.

a01.question: Which ion has more electrons than protons and more protons than neutrons? [H = ¹₁H; D = ²₁H; O = ¹⁶₈O]
a01.explanation: OH⁻: 9 protons, 8 neutrons, 10 electrons.

a01.question: In which pairs do both species have the same number of unpaired p electrons? (1) Al²⁻ and O⁺ (2) N and Cl²⁺ (3) C and Cl⁺
a01.explanation: Al²⁻/O⁺ are p^3; N/Cl²⁺ are p^3; C/Cl⁺ are p^2.

a01.question: First six ionisation energies (kJ mol⁻¹). Which element is most likely in Group 14?  A: 494, 4560, 6940, 9540, 13400, 16600  B: 736, 1450, 7740, 10500, 13600, 18000  C: 1090, 2350, 4610, 6220, 37800, 47000  D: 1400, 2860, 4590, 7480, 9400, 53200
a01.explanation: Four outer electrons means a large jump between the 4th and 5th IE (6220 → 37800).

a01.question: Which statements are correct when referring to the atoms ²³Na and ²⁴Mg? (1) They have the same number of full electron orbitals. (2) They have the same number of neutrons. (3) They are both reducing agents.
a01.explanation: Both have 12 neutrons. Na has 5 full orbitals, Mg has 6.

a01.question: In which set do all species contain the same number of electrons?
a01.explanation: Na⁺, Mg²⁺ and Al³⁺ each have 10 electrons.

a01.question: X is a particle with 18 electrons and 20 neutrons. What could it be? (1) ³⁸₁₈Ar (2) ⁴⁰₂₀Ca²⁺ (3) ³⁹₁₉K⁺
a01.explanation: All have 18 electrons and 20 neutrons.

a01.question: Carbon and nitrogen are adjacent in the Periodic Table. Which properties do they both have? (1) There is an empty 2p orbital in each atom of the element. (2) The principal quantum number of the highest occupied orbital is 2. (3) They can form compounds in which their atoms form four bonds.
a01.explanation: N (2p^3) has no empty 2p orbital. CH₄ and NH₄⁺ both show four bonds.

a01.question: X⁻ ions can be oxidised to X by acidified KMnO₄. What could be the first four ionisation energies of X?  A: 418, 3070, 4600, 5860  B: 577, 1820, 2740, 11600  C: 590, 1150, 4940, 6480  D: 1010, 1840, 2040, 4030
a01.explanation: X is a halogen (Group 17), whose first IE is about 1000 kJ mol⁻¹.

a01.question: The graph shows first ionisation energy against proton number. Which statement is correct?
a01.option_a: Elements Q and Y are in the same period.
a01.option_b: The general increase from R to Y is due to increasing atomic radius.
a01.option_c: The small decrease between S and T is due to decreased shielding.
a01.option_d: The small decrease between V and W is due to repulsion between paired electrons.
a01.explanation: V to W is P to S: the first paired p electron. Q and Y are in different periods and the increase is due to nuclear charge.
a01.alt: Graph of first ionisation energy against proton number with labelled points Q to Y.

a01.question: The ¹₁H₃⁺ ion and the ⁶Li⁺ ion: which statements are correct? (1) Both ions contain the same number of protons. (2) Both ions contain the same number of electrons. (3) Both ions contain the same number of neutrons.
a01.explanation: Both have 3 protons and 2 electrons. H₃⁺ has no neutrons; ⁶Li⁺ has 3.

a01.question: Atoms of element X have six unpaired electrons. What could X be?
a01.explanation: Cr is [Ar]3d^5 4s^1.

a01.question: The graph shows the relative first IE of four elements with consecutive atomic numbers (A–D). One reacts with hydrogen to form covalent HX. Which could be X?
a01.explanation: B is a noble gas and C is Group 1, so A is a halogen and forms HX.
a01.alt: Four points: A high, B the highest, C very low, D slightly above C.

a01.question: What could be the composition of an H₃⁺ ion?
a01.explanation: Three ¹H nuclei and 3 − 1 = 2 electrons.

a01.question: Flerovium (Z = 114, nucleon no. 289) and livermorium (Z = 116, nucleon no. 292). Which statements are correct? (1) One atom of Lv has one more neutron than one atom of Fl. (2) One Fl²⁻ ion has the same number of electrons as one atom of Lv. (3) One Lv⁺ ion has the same number of electrons as one Fl⁻ ion.
a01.explanation: Neutrons 175 and 176. Fl²⁻ = 116 e; Lv⁺ = 115 e = Fl⁻.

a01.question: Which ions contain one or more unpaired electrons? (1) Cu²⁺ (2) Mn³⁺ (3) V³⁺
a01.explanation: Cu²⁺ d^9, Mn³⁺ d^4, V³⁺ d^2.

a01.question: Which ion is not isoelectronic with K⁺?
a01.explanation: K⁺ has 18 e; Ti³⁺ has 19.

a01.question: Which statements are correct when referring to the two common isotopes of chlorine? (1) The isotopes have different masses. (2) The isotopes have different numbers of nucleons. (3) The isotopes have the same chemical reactions.
a01.explanation: Isotopes differ in neutrons only; the electrons (and so the chemistry) are the same.

a01.question: Which statements are correct when referring to the isotopes of a single element? (1) The isotopes have different masses. (2) The isotopes have different numbers of nucleons. (3) The isotopes have different chemical reactions.
a01.explanation: Chemical reactions depend on electrons, which are the same.

a01.question: In which option do all three particles have the same electronic configuration and the same number of neutrons?
a01.explanation: Each of ¹⁸O²⁻, ¹⁹F⁻, ²⁰Ne has 10 e and 10 n.

a01.question: Which statements about ³¹P³⁻ and ³⁵Cl⁻ are correct? (1) They have the same number of electrons. (2) They have the same number of neutrons. (3) They have the same number of protons.
a01.explanation: Both have 18 e; neutrons 16 and 18; protons 15 and 17.

a01.question: F⁻, Ne and Na⁺ are isoelectronic. In which order do their radii increase?
a01.explanation: Same electrons, more protons gives a smaller radius: Na⁺ < Ne < F⁻.

a01.question: Successive IEs (kJ mol⁻¹) of X are 950, 1800, 2700, 4800, 6000, 12300. What could be a chloride of X?
a01.explanation: The jump after the 5th IE shows Group 15, forming XCl₃.

a01.question: Which statements about orbitals in a krypton atom are correct? (1) The 1s and 2s orbitals have the same energy but different sizes. (2) The third energy level has three subshells and nine orbitals. (3) The 3d subshell has five orbitals of the same energy in an isolated atom.
a01.explanation: 1s and 2s differ in energy. n = 3 has 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 orbitals.

a01.question: The M_r of a sample of chlorine is 72.0. Which properties of the atoms in this sample are the same for all of them? (1) radius (2) nucleon number (3) isotopic mass
a01.explanation: The sample contains ³⁵Cl and ³⁷Cl; their electron structure and radius are the same.

a01.question: Which of the following influence the size of the ionisation energy of an atom? (1) the amount of shielding by the inner electrons (2) the charge on the nucleus (3) the distance between the outer electrons and the nucleus
a01.explanation: All three factors matter.

a01.question: ²³⁸₉₂U reacts with deuterium ²₁H to give an isotope J and two neutrons. What is J?
a01.explanation: Nucleons 238 + 2 = J + 2 gives 238; protons 92 + 1 = 93 is neptunium.

a01.question: Three of these configurations belong to Cl, Na and V. Which belongs to another element?
a01.explanation: D has 26 electrons: iron.

a01.question: X and Y are in the same group. First six IEs (kJ mol⁻¹): X 800, 1600, 2400, 4300, 5400, 10400; Y 1000, 1800, 2700, 4800, 6000, 12300. What could X and Y be?
a01.explanation: Group 15 (jump after the 5th). IE falls down the group, so X (lower) is Sb.

a01.question: Which isolated gaseous atom has a total of five electrons in spherical orbitals?
Carbon and silicon have the same outer electronic structure. Why is a Si–Si bond weaker than a C–C bond?
a01.option_a: Silicon atoms have a larger atomic radius.
a01.option_b: Silicon has a greater nuclear charge.
a01.option_c: Silicon has a smaller first ionisation energy.
a01.explanation: Larger atoms overlap less well, so the bond is longer and weaker.

a01.question: Compound X is made from two elements, one with the second highest first IE in its group and the other the third highest in its group. Which could be X? (1) calcium chloride (2) magnesium bromide (3) potassium sulfide
a01.explanation: Ca is 3rd in Group 2 and Cl is 2nd in Group 17; Mg 2nd, Br 3rd; K 3rd, S 2nd.

a01.question: For sulfur, which pair of ionisation energies has the largest difference?
a01.explanation: S has six outer electrons; the 7th comes from an inner shell.

a01.question: Which species contains the smallest number of electrons?
a01.explanation: The first three each have 2 e; He⁺ has 1.

a01.question: Which property of an atom does not affect its first ionisation energy?
a01.explanation: Neutrons are not involved in the attraction to electrons.

a01.question: Deflection is proportional to charge/mass. Protons deflect +15°; particle Y deflects −5°. What could be the composition of Y? Row 1: 1 p, 2 n, 2 e. Row 2: 3 p, 3 n, 5 e. Row 3: 4 p, 5 n, 1 e. (1) Row 1 (2) Row 2 (3) Row 3
a01.explanation: Y must be negative with charge/mass −1/3: rows 1 (−1/3) and 2 (−2/6). Row 3 is positive.

a01.question: An isolated gaseous atom X has paired electrons in at least one 3d orbital and a filled 4s subshell. What could X be? (1) iron (2) gallium (3) copper
a01.explanation: Fe is 3d^6 4s^2; Ga is 3d¹⁰ 4s^2 4p^1; Cu is 3d¹⁰ 4s^1.

a01.question: The ion Y³⁻ has 18 electrons and mass number 31. How many protons and neutrons?
a01.explanation: Protons 18 − 3 = 15; neutrons 31 − 15 = 16.

a01.question: In which pair do the atoms contain the same number of neutrons?
a01.explanation: Both ¹¹B and ¹²C have 6 neutrons.

a01.question: The two outermost shells of an atom are 3s^2 3p^6 3d^5 4s^2. What is this atom?
a01.explanation: Total electrons = 25: manganese.

a01.question: How many electrons are in a hydrogencarbonate anion, HCO₃⁻?
In which isolated gaseous atom are all electrons paired?
a01.explanation: Group 2 Ba has only filled subshells.

a01.question: X has a higher first IE than Y. Student 1: X has more protons. Student 2: X has a smaller radius. Only one student is correct. What could X and Y be?
a01.explanation: O has a higher IE than S because of its smaller radius, but it has fewer protons.

a01.question: Which element has the second smallest atomic radius in its group and the third lowest first IE in its period?
a01.explanation: Mg is second in Group 2 and third lowest in Period 3 (Na < Al < Mg).

a01.question: A sulfur atom is 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^4. How many valence shell and unpaired electrons does it have?
a01.explanation: 3s^2 3p^4 gives 6 valence electrons, 2 unpaired.

a01.question: Neutrons are passed through an electric field. What is the neutron's relative mass and behaviour?
a01.explanation: A neutron has relative mass 1 and no charge.

a01.question: For the second shell of an atom with eight protons, which row is correct?
a01.option_a: dumbbell: p, 2 e; spherical: s, 4 e
a01.option_b: dumbbell: p, 4 e; spherical: s, 2 e
a01.option_c: dumbbell: s, 2 e; spherical: p, 4 e
a01.option_d: dumbbell: s, 4 e; spherical: p, 2 e
a01.explanation: O is 2s^2 2p^4; p orbitals are dumbbell-shaped.

a01.question: Which statement describes the C–H bond in ethene?
a01.option_a: a π bond between an s orbital and an sp^2 orbital
a01.option_b: a π bond between an s orbital and an sp^3 orbital
a01.option_c: a σ bond between an s orbital and an sp^2 orbital
a01.option_d: a σ bond between an s orbital and an sp^3 orbital
a01.explanation: Each carbon is sp^2 and forms a σ bond with H 1s.

a01.question: Rubidium and bromine form isoelectronic ions with 36 electrons. Which row is correct?
a01.option_a: Rb: atomic < ionic; Br: atomic < ionic
a01.option_b: Rb: atomic < ionic; Br: atomic > ionic
a01.option_c: Rb: atomic > ionic; Br: atomic < ionic
a01.option_d: Rb: atomic > ionic; Br: atomic > ionic
a01.explanation: Rb loses an electron (smaller); Br gains one (larger).

a01.question: IEs of X are 577, 1980, 2960, 6190 kJ mol⁻¹. Which ion of X is produced by removing an electron from a filled shell?
a01.explanation: X has three outer electrons; the 4th comes from a filled inner shell.

a01.question: Which statement about a 3p orbital is correct?
a01.option_a: It can hold a maximum of 6 electrons.
a01.option_b: It has the highest energy of the orbitals with n = 3.
a01.option_c: It is at a higher energy level than 3s but has the same shape.
a01.option_d: It is occupied by one electron in an isolated phosphorus atom.
a01.explanation: P is 3p^3, one electron in each 3p orbital.

a01.question: In which pairs do both species have the same number of unpaired p electrons? (1) O and Cl⁺ (2) F⁺ and Ga⁻ (3) N and Kr³⁺
a01.explanation: O and Cl⁺ have 2; F⁺ and Ga⁻ have 2; N and Kr³⁺ have 3.

a01.question: The outermost electron in neon occupies which orbital? (energy and shape)
a01.explanation: Ne is 2p^6, a dumbbell-shaped orbital.

a01.question: In which species is there a lone pair of electrons?
a01.explanation: CH₃⁻ has three bond pairs and one lone pair.

a01.question: An atom of calcium-48 forms a 2+ ion. Which statements are correct? (1) It has 20 protons. (2) It has 28 neutrons. (3) It has 22 electrons.
a01.explanation: Ca²⁺ has 18 electrons.

a01.question: W, X, Y and Z have configurations 2,4; 2,6; 2,8,2 and 2,8,8,1. Which formulae are compounds with boiling points below room temperature? (1) WX₂ (2) YX (3) Z₂X
a01.explanation: CO₂ is simple molecular; MgO and K₂O are ionic.

a01.question: Graphs of successive IEs for two Period 3 elements: P has a big jump after the 7th electron, Q after the 2nd. What is the ionic compound formed?
a01.explanation: P is Cl (7 outer electrons) and Q is Mg (2).
a01.alt: Two graphs of successive ionisation energies: P with a jump after electron 7, Q after electron 2.

a01.question: Which orbital overlap forms the σ bond between the two carbons in ethene?
a01.option_c: end-on overlap of two sp^2 hybrid orbitals
a01.option_d: sideways overlap of two p orbitals
a01.explanation: The C–C σ bond is head-on sp^2–sp^2; sideways p–p overlap makes the π bond.

a01.question: Which atom has exactly three unpaired electrons in the ground state?
a01.explanation: P is 3p^3.

a01.question: Which deductions about the ²⁰⁹₈₃Bi atom are correct? (1) It has 83 electrons. (2) It has 126 nucleons. (3) It has 83 neutrons.
a01.explanation: 209 nucleons and 126 neutrons.

a01.question: Which statements about ⁷⁰₃₂Ge are correct? (1) It has the same number of electrons as ⁷⁹₃₄Se²⁺. (2) It has the same number of neutrons as ⁶⁸₃₀Zn. (3) It has half as many protons as ¹⁶⁰₆₄Gd.
a01.explanation: Se²⁺ has 32 e; both have 38 neutrons; 32 is half of 64.

a01.question: The first IE of chlorine is greater than that of sulfur. Which factors contribute? (1) Chlorine has more protons. (2) Chlorine has greater electron shielding. (3) The covalent bonds in Cl₂ are stronger than in S.
a01.explanation: Cl has a higher nuclear charge with similar shielding.

a01.question: The graph shows successive IEs of X (dashed) and Y (solid), both in Period 3. Which statement is correct?
a01.option_a: X needs one extra electron for a full shell; Y needs three.
a01.option_b: Y has five electrons in the 3p subshell.
a01.option_c: X has oxidation number +7 in most of its compounds.
a01.option_d: X combined with Y gives ionic bonding.
a01.explanation: X (jump after 7) is Cl; Y (jump after 5) is P (3p^3).
a01.alt: Successive IEs 1 to 10: dashed X rises steeply after the 7th, solid Y after the 5th.

a01.question: Which statement about the electrons in ground state carbon is correct?
a01.option_a: Electrons are present in four energy levels.
a01.option_b: More electrons are in p orbitals than s orbitals.
a01.option_c: The occupied orbital of highest energy is spherical.
a01.option_d: The occupied orbital of lowest energy is spherical.
a01.explanation: 1s is the lowest orbital and is spherical.

a01.question: How many protons, neutrons and electrons are in ⁵⁴Fe³⁺? (Z = 26)
For which hydrocarbon are the molecular and empirical formulae the same?
a01.explanation: C₃H₈ cannot be simplified.

a01.question: In which pair does each species have the same number of unpaired electrons?
Fifth to eighth IEs (kJ mol⁻¹). Which row refers to chlorine?  A: 6280, 21200, 25900, 30500  B: 6990, 8490, 27100, 31700  C: 6540, 9330, 11000, 33600  D: 7240, 8790, 12000, 13800
a01.explanation: Cl has 7 outer electrons: the jump is between the 7th and 8th.

a01.question: Element 119 is predicted to be a Group 1 element in Period 8. Which predictions are likely correct? (1) The outermost occupied orbital will be an s orbital. (2) The atomic radius will be the largest in Group 1. (3) It will have a greater first IE than element 118.
a01.explanation: A noble gas has a far higher first IE.

a01.question: Na (Z = 11, A = 23) and F (Z = 9, A = 19). Which statements about the atoms and ions are correct? (1) One Na atom has two more protons than one F⁻ ion. (2) One Na atom has two more neutrons than one F atom. (3) One Na⁺ ion has the same number of electrons as one F⁻ ion.
a01.explanation: Protons 11 vs 9; neutrons 12 vs 10; both ions have 10 e.

a01.question: Which particle has equal numbers of protons and neutrons and the structure 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6?
a01.explanation: ⁴⁰Ca²⁺: 20 p, 20 n, 18 e.

a01.question: Which molecule contains six bonding electrons?
a01.explanation: NCl₃ has three single bonds.

a01.question: What is the electronic configuration of an isolated Ni²⁺ ion?
a01.explanation: Ni is [Ar]3d^8 4s^2; the 4s electrons go first.

a01.question: A ³²P nucleus forms when a ³²S nucleus joins with particle X and a proton is emitted. What is X?
a01.explanation: Nucleons: 32 + a = 32 + 1 so a = 1; protons: 16 + z = 15 + 1 so z = 0.

a01.question: Which atomic orbitals are occupied in a phosphorus atom?
a01.explanation: P is 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p; there is no 1p, 2d or occupied 3d.

a01.question: Particles W, X, Y, Z (protons, neutrons, electrons): W 32, 40, 32; X 32, 40, 34; Y 32, 42, 32; Z 34, 40, 34. Which pair represents atoms of two isotopes of the same element?
a01.explanation: Same protons, different neutrons, neutral atoms.

a01.question: Where is the element with outer configuration 4s^2 4p^3?
a01.explanation: Five outer electrons and n = 4 gives arsenic.

a01.question: In which pair do both species have only one unpaired p electron?
a01.explanation: F (2p^5) and Ga (4p^1) have one each.

a01.question: Why is the first IE of oxygen less than that of nitrogen?
a01.option_a: N has its outer electron in a different subshell.
a01.option_b: O has the greater nuclear charge.
a01.option_c: O has a pair of electrons in one p orbital that repel one another.
a01.option_d: There is more shielding in O.
a01.explanation: Paired-electron repulsion in the 2p orbital makes one easier to remove.

a01.question: Which equation represents the first ionisation energy of iodine?
a01.explanation: One mole of electrons removed from one mole of gaseous atoms.

a01.question: In which ions is the number of electrons equal to the number of neutrons? (1) ¹⁹₉F⁻ (2) ³¹₁₅P⁻ (3) ²³₁₁Na⁺
Which atom has the same number of electrons as an ammonium ion?
a01.explanation: NH₄⁺ has 10 electrons.

a01.question: Which statements about first ionisation energies are correct? (1) They are always endothermic. (2) They decrease down Group 2. (3) They decrease across Period 3.
a01.explanation: IE generally rises across a period.

a01.question: Which of these has the highest fifth ionisation energy?
a01.explanation: Carbon has 4 outer electrons; the 5th is from the 1s shell.

a01.question: X²⁺ has the same configuration as Kr. What is the configuration of an atom of X?
a01.explanation: X has 38 electrons (Sr).

a01.question: A technetium isotope has 56 neutrons (Z = 43). What is its nucleon number?
Which atom has more unpaired than paired electrons in orbitals with n = 2?
a01.explanation: N: 2s^2 (2 paired) and 2p^3 (3 unpaired).

a01.question: The first IE of K is 418 and of Sr is 548 kJ mol⁻¹. Which statement explains why Sr is greater?
a01.option_a: The charge on the Sr nucleus is greater.
a01.option_b: The outer electron in Sr experiences greater shielding.
a01.option_c: The outer electron in Sr experiences spin-pair repulsion.
a01.option_d: The outer electron in Sr is further from the nucleus.
a01.explanation: Sr has 38 protons against 19 with similar shielding.

a01.question: What is the electronic configuration of Mg²⁺?
a01.explanation: Mg loses its two 3s electrons.

a01.question: Which atom has its outermost electron in a dumbbell-shaped orbital with n = 3?
a01.explanation: A dumbbell is p; Cl is 3p^5.

a01.question: Which atom has the same number of electrons as OH⁻?
a01.explanation: OH⁻ has 10 electrons.

a01.question: J and L are in Group 15; both form covalent hydrides (oxidation number −3). Hydrogen bonding occurs only in L's hydride. Which row could be correct?
a01.explanation: Only NH₃ hydrogen bonds; Group 15 is ns^2 np^3.

a01.question: Which element has the second smallest atomic radius in its group and the second highest electrical conductivity in its period?
a01.explanation: Mg is second in Group 2 and Al > Mg > Na in Period 3.

a01.question: Which atom contains four times as many neutrons as ⁷₃Li?
a01.explanation: Li has 4 neutrons; ³¹P has 16.

a01.question: Which statement about the first IEs of magnesium and neon is correct?
a01.explanation: Ionisation always needs energy; Ne is about 2080 vs Mg 738.

a01.question: (1) The atomic radius of K is greater than that of Cl; (2) the first IE of K is greater than that of Cl; (3) the ionic radius of K⁺ is greater than that of Cl⁻. Which are correct?
a01.explanation: K⁺ is smaller than Cl⁻ and K has a lower IE.

a01.question: Fifth to eighth IEs of Period 3 element E are 16000, 20000, 24000, 29000 kJ mol⁻¹. In which group is E?
a01.explanation: The big jump comes between the 4th and 5th: Si.

a01.question: The diagram shows melting points of eight elements with consecutive atomic numbers. Which could be sodium?
a01.explanation: The sequence F, Ne, Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S fits; sodium is the third point.
a01.alt: Melting point against atomic number for eight elements: A slightly above B, then rising through C and D to a peak, then falling.

a01.question: ³⁵Cl⁺ ions are detected in a mass spectrometer. How many neutrons and what configuration does ³⁵Cl⁺ have?
a01.explanation: Neutrons 35 − 17 = 18; Cl⁺ has 16 electrons (3p^4).

a01.question: Which species is a free radical?
a01.explanation: Be⁻ (2p^1) has an unpaired electron.

a01.question: Which statement is correct?
a01.option_a: The first IE of Cl is more than that of Ar.
a01.option_b: The second IE of Ca is more than that of Mg.
a01.option_c: The second IE of S equals the first IE of P.
a01.option_d: The eighth IE of Cl is more than the first IE of Ne.
a01.explanation: The 8th IE of Cl is removed from an inner shell (~33600).

a01.question: Which molecule contains the same total number of valence electrons as HCN?

a02.question: Anhydrous CaCl₂ absorbs water to form CaCl₂.2H₂O. What is the percentage increase in mass?

What is the ionic equation for aqueous sodium carbonate and dilute nitric acid?
a02.explanation: Nitric acid is a strong acid (H⁺); spectator ions are omitted.

a02.question: 1.00 g of carbon burns in limited oxygen: 0.50 g forms CO₂ and 0.50 g forms CO. The mixture is passed through excess NaOH(aq) and the remaining gas collected. What is its volume at 25 °C and 1 atm (1 mol = 24 dm^3)?
a02.explanation: NaOH removes CO₂. CO from 0.50 g C = 0.0417 mol × 24 = 1.0 dm^3.

a02.question: An egg shell is 5% of a 50 g egg and is pure CaCO₃. How many complete shells neutralise 50 cm^3 of 2.0 mol dm⁻³ ethanoic acid?
a02.explanation: Acid 0.10 mol needs 0.05 mol CaCO₃ = 5.0 g; a shell is 2.5 g.

a02.question: S₂O₇ is hydrolysed to sulfuric acid and oxygen only. What volume of O₂ (room conditions) forms from 0.352 g of S₂O₇?
a02.explanation: 2S₂O₇ + 4H₂O → 4H₂SO₄ + O₂; n = 0.002 mol so n(O₂) = 0.001 mol = 24 cm^3.

a02.question: What is the percentage by mass of carbon in tetraethyl lead, Pb(C₂H₅)₄?

A mixture of MgO and Al₂O₃: 100 cm^3 of 2 mol dm⁻³ NaOH just dissolves the Al₂O₃ in x g (Al₂O₃ + 2OH⁻ + 3H₂O → 2Al(OH)₄⁻). 800 cm^3 of 2 mol dm⁻³ HCl just dissolves all the oxide in x g. How many moles of each oxide?
a02.explanation: n(OH⁻) = 0.20 so Al₂O₃ = 0.10 mol. H⁺ = 1.6 mol; Al₂O₃ uses 0.6, leaving 1.0 for MgO (0.50 mol).

a02.question: A 2.00 g rock containing CaCO₃ neutralises exactly 36.0 cm^3 of 0.500 mol dm⁻³ HCl. What % of the rock is CaCO₃?
Blood glucose C₆H₁₂O₆ is 18.5 mmol/l in China. Convert to mg/dl (dl = 0.1 dm^3).
a02.explanation: 18.5 mmol × 180 = 3330 mg per litre = 333 mg per dl.

a02.question: 10 cm^3 of gaseous organic compound J was sparked with excess O₂ giving 20 cm^3 CO₂ and 5 cm^3 N₂ (same T and p). What could J be? (1) C₂H₆N₂ (2) C₂H₃N (3) C₂H₇N
a02.explanation: Each molecule has 2 C and 1 N (0.5 N₂).

a02.question: Which mass of urea, CO(NH₂)₂, contains the same mass of N as 101.1 g of KNO₃?
a02.explanation: 101.1 g KNO₃ = 1 mol = 14 g N; urea is 28 g N per 60 g.

a02.question: The relative atomic mass of copper is 63.5. Which chart is a correct mass spectrum that would lead to this value?
What volume of O₂ (room conditions) burns 1.0 mol of methylpropan-1-ol completely? (1 mol = 24 dm^3)
Lithium is 7.42% ⁶Li and 92.58% ⁷Li. What is the relative atomic mass to 3 s.f.?
A medal of area 150 cm^2 gains 0.216 g of silver. How many silver atoms per cm^2? (A_r Ag = 107.9)
Which contains 9.03 × 10²³ oxygen atoms?
2.00 dm^3 of N₂ reacts with excess H₂; only 15.0% reacts. What mass of NH₃ forms? (room conditions)
a02.explanation: n(N₂) = 0.0125 mol so n(NH₃) = 0.025 mol = 0.425 g.

a02.question: 0.216 g of an aluminium compound X reacts with water giving a hydrocarbon that burns to give 108 cm^3 CO₂ at room conditions. What is X?
a02.explanation: n(CH₄) = 4.5 × 10⁻³ mol; Al₄C₃ (M_r 144) 1.5 × 10⁻³ mol gives 3 CH₄ each.

a02.question: Which formula represents the empirical formula of a compound?

a02.explanation: CO₂ = 600 cm^3; HCl 0.05 mol = 250 cm^3; NaCl 0.05 mol = 2.93 g.

a02.question: C_WH_X and C_YH_Z are hydrocarbons with W, X, Y, Z different whole numbers and W/X = Y/Z. Which row is correct?
a02.option_a: empirical different; molecular same; M_r different
a02.option_b: empirical different; molecular same; M_r same
a02.option_c: empirical same; molecular different; M_r different
a02.option_d: empirical same; molecular different; M_r same
a02.explanation: Same C:H ratio but different numbers give different molecular formulae and M_r.

a02.question: [H⁺] is 1.26 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ in 11 000 dm^3. What mass of solid NaOH neutralises it?
Compound Q contains 40% carbon by mass. What could it be? (1) glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆ (2) starch, (C₆H₁₀O₅)_n (3) sucrose, C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁
Which fuel gives the largest mass of CO₂ per 10 kg?

1 mol H₂SO₄ gives a solution containing H₂SO₄, H⁺, SO₄²⁻ and HSO₄⁻. Which statements are correct? (1) It contains 6.02 × 10²³ sulfur atoms. (2) It contains exactly equal numbers of H⁺ and HSO₄⁻ ions. (3) One mole of SO₄²⁻ contains two moles of electrons.
a02.explanation: H⁺ also comes from HSO₄⁻ dissociating; SO₄²⁻ has 50 electrons.

a02.question: Compound J burns to CO₂ and H₂O only: 3.00 g gives 4.40 g CO₂ and 1.80 g H₂O. What is its empirical formula?
1 mol of an organic compound X needs 2.5 mol O₂ for complete combustion. Which could X be? (1) C₂H₅OH (2) C₂H₂ (3) CH₃CHO

Three samples each contain 0.710 g Cl₂ and react with (a) H₂, (b) cold NaOH, (c) hot NaOH. Which product masses are correct? (1) 0.730 g HCl in the first reaction. (2) 0.585 g NaCl in the second. (3) 0.975 g NaCl in the third.
a02.explanation: 0.0100 mol Cl₂: 0.0200 mol HCl; 0.0100 mol NaCl; 3Cl₂ → 5NaCl gives 0.0167 mol.

a02.question: C₇H₆O₃ (M_r 138.0) + C₄H₆O₃ (M_r 102.0) → C₉H₈O₄ (aspirin, 180.0) + C₂H₄O₂. 10.0 g of each reactant: maximum mass of aspirin?
Combustion of a hydrocarbon gave 0.132 g CO₂ and 0.054 g H₂O. Which formulae could it be? (1) CH₂=CH₂ (2) CH₃CH=CH₂ (3) CH₃CH=CHCH₃
Under room conditions 600 cm^3 of gas X has a mass of 0.700 g. What could X be? (1) carbon monoxide (2) ethene (3) nitrogen
C₆H₁₂ is burned in dry oxygen; H₂O is absorbed in CaCl₂ (increase M_P) and CO₂ in soda lime (M_Q). What is M_P/M_Q?
5.0 g samples of the carbonates of Ba, Cu(II), Li and Mg are decomposed. For which is the mass loss greatest?
a02.explanation: Lowest M_r gives most CO₂: Li₂CO₃ 73.8.

a02.question: Deflection is proportional to charge/mass. Protons deflect +15°. What is the angle for ²H⁻ ions?
a02.explanation: q/m is −1/2 that of a proton.

a02.question: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. Which statements are correct? (1) 3.27 g Zn with excess HCl gives 0.0500 mol ZnCl₂. (2) 6.54 g Zn reacts with exactly 100 cm^3 of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl. (3) 13.08 g Zn gives 9.60 dm^3 H₂ at room conditions.
a02.explanation: 6.54 g needs 200 cm^3; 13.08 g gives 4.80 dm^3.

a02.question: 3.7 g of CuCO₃ is added to 25 cm^3 of 2.0 mol dm⁻³ HCl. What volume of gas forms under room conditions?
a02.explanation: HCl is limiting: 0.050 mol HCl gives 0.025 mol CO₂ = 0.60 dm^3.

a02.question: 1.00 g of washing powder needs 7.15 cm^3 of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ to react with its NaHCO₃. What is the % NaHCO₃?
One carat is 0.200 g of carbon. Which expression gives the carats containing 6.02 × 10²³ carbon atoms?

2NaN₃ → 2Na + 3N₂. What volume of N₂ (room conditions) comes from 150 g NaN₃?
a02.explanation: 2.31 mol NaN₃ gives 3.46 mol N₂ = 83 dm^3.

a02.question: NH₄Cl(s) decomposes to NH₃ + HCl. A total of 2.4 × 10²¹ gas molecules forms. How many H atoms are in the products?

6SrO + 2Al → 3Sr + Sr₃Al₂O₆. What mass of Sr can 100 g of SrO produce?
An ore contains 4% MnO₂. What mass of Mn from 1 tonne?

Which contains the largest number of hydrogen atoms?

a02.explanation: 0.50 mol C₃H₈ needs 2.5 mol O₂ = 80 g.

a02.question: C₂H₅OH + CH₃CO₂H ⇌ CH₃CO₂C₂H₅ + H₂O, ΔH = −6 kJ mol⁻¹. 9.2 g ethanol, 12 g ethanoic acid and 8.8 g ester stand at 298 K; equilibrium contains 4.8 g ethanoic acid. a02.explanation: Acid used 0.12 mol so ester 0.22 mol. Exothermic: higher T moves left. K_c depends on T only.

a02.question: A gaseous hydrocarbon has density 2.42 g dm⁻³ under room conditions. Which could it be? (1 = butane; 2 = methylcyclopropane; 3 = but-2-ene)
Which statement about the Avogadro constant is correct?
a02.option_a: The mass of one mole of any element.
a02.option_b: The mass of 6.02 × 10²³ atoms of any element.
a02.option_c: The number of atoms in one mole of neon.
a02.option_d: The number of atoms in 12 g of any element.

a02.question: Compound X is a straight chain hydrocarbon with M_r 84. What can be determined? (1) empirical formula (2) molecular formula (3) whether X contains a C=C bond
a02.explanation: M_r 84 is C₆H₁₂: empirical CH₂, and a straight chain C₆H₁₂ must have C=C.

a02.question: X contains 30.6% C, 3.8% H, 20.4% O and 45.2% Cl by mass. What is its empirical formula?

a02.explanation: 0.025 mol gives 0.050 mol H₂O: NH₄NO₃ → N₂O + 2H₂O.

a02.question: X is 40.0% C, 6.7% H, 53.3% O by mass. What is its empirical formula?
Which statement is correct?

a02.option_a: The molecular formula is the simplest whole number ratio of atoms.
a02.option_b: One mole of any substance contains 6 × 10²³ atoms.
a02.option_c: Relative atomic mass is the ratio of the average mass of an atom to the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
a02.option_d: Relative formula mass is the sum of the individual atomic masses of all the atoms in the formula.

a02.question: 5.0 g of each of four s-block metals is added to excess water. Which gives the largest volume of gas?
a02.explanation: Ca gives 0.125 mol H₂ (K 0.064, Rb 0.029, Sr 0.057).

a02.question: 1 mol Cu with concentrated HNO₃ gives 1 mol Cu(NO₃)₂, 2 mol H₂O and X only. What could X be?

a02.explanation: MgS uses 0.050 mol H⁺; 0.075 mol left so 0.0375 mol CaO = 2.1 g.

a02.question: Molten aluminium chloride is Al₂Cl₆ molecules. Which statement is correct?
a02.option_a: All Cl atoms in 1 g have the same mass.

a02.question: 3.10 g of CoSO₄.xH₂O loses 1.39 g on heating. What is x?
Which statement is correct?
a02.option_a: The relative atomic mass of ³⁵Cl is 35.5.
a02.option_b: The relative formula mass of CaCO₃ is 100.1.
a02.option_c: The relative isotopic mass of ²⁴Mg is 24.3.
a02.option_d: The relative molecular mass of O₂ is 16.0.

a02.option_a: Cl has a relative isotopic mass of 35.5.

a03.question: Which element is likely to have an electronegativity similar to aluminium?
a03.explanation: Be and Al are diagonal neighbours (about 1.5).

a03.question: What is involved when a hydrogen bond forms between two molecules? (1) a hydrogen atom bonded to an atom less electronegative than itself (2) a lone pair of electrons (3) an electrostatic attraction between opposite charges
a03.explanation: H must be bonded to N, O or F and attracted to a lone pair.

a03.question: In H₃C–N=C=O, what is the approximate angle between the bonds formed by the N atom?
a03.explanation: N has three regions of electron density: about 120°.

a03.question: Why does Al₂Cl₆ sublime at a low temperature? (1) The intermolecular forces between the Al₂Cl₆ molecules are weak. (2) The co-ordinate bonds between Al and Cl are weak. (3) The covalent bonds between Al and Cl are weak.
a03.explanation: Only the weak forces between molecules are overcome.

a03.question: Which can be explained by hydrogen bonding? (1) Ice floats on water. (2) The boiling point of propan-2-ol (82 °C) is higher than that of propanone (56 °C). (3) Propanone and propanal mix completely.
a03.explanation: Propanone and propanal cannot hydrogen bond with each other.

a03.question: Which types of dipole explain Br₂ and CHCl₃ being liquids at room temperature?
a03.option_a: Br₂: induced and permanent; CHCl₃: induced and permanent
a03.option_b: Br₂: induced and permanent; CHCl₃: induced only
a03.option_c: Br₂: induced only; CHCl₃: induced and permanent
a03.option_d: Br₂: induced only; CHCl₃: induced only
a03.explanation: Br₂ is non-polar; CHCl₃ is polar.

a03.question: Which statements about bond angles are correct? (1) SO₃ is smaller than CO₂. (2) H₂O is smaller than CH₄. (3) NH₃ is smaller than BF₃.
P: mp 2852 °C, conducts when liquid, insoluble. Q: mp 993 °C, conducts when liquid and in solution. R: mp −119 °C, bp 39 °C, never conducts. What could they be?
a03.explanation: Ionic oxide, ionic fluoride, simple molecular liquid.

a03.question: NH₄⁺ → NH₃ and C₂H₄ → C₂H₆ share which similar feature?
a03.option_a: a lone pair in the product

a03.question: AlCl₃ catalyses RCl + AlCl₃ → R⁺ + AlCl₄⁻. Which property makes this possible?
a03.option_a: It exists as Al₂Cl₆ in the vapour.
a03.option_c: The aluminium atom has an incomplete octet.
a03.option_d: Cl in RCl has a vacant p orbital.
a03.explanation: Al has six outer electrons and accepts a lone pair.

a03.question: Why is NCl₅ not possible? (1) Nitrogen's outer shell can only contain eight electrons. (2) Nitrogen cannot have oxidation state +5. (3) Nitrogen is almost inert.
a03.explanation: N has no 2d orbitals but can be +5 (HNO₃).

a03.question: What is always involved in a carbon–carbon π bond? (1) a shared pair of electrons (2) sideways overlap of p orbitals (3) delocalised electrons
What is the predicted H–N–N angle in hydrazine, H₂N–NH₂?
a03.explanation: Three bond pairs and a lone pair: pyramidal.

a03.question: Which solid contains more than one kind of bonding?
a03.explanation: Covalent within molecules, van der Waals between.

a03.question: Which have a regular trigonal planar shape? (1) BF₃ (2) CH₃⁺ (3) AlCl₃
a03.explanation: Three bond pairs, no lone pairs.

a03.question: What are the shapes around B in BH₄⁻ and BF₃?
a03.explanation: Four bond pairs; three bond pairs.

a03.question: In which pair do the molecules have the same shape?
a03.explanation: Both bent (2 bond pairs, 2 lone pairs).

a03.question: How may nitrogen exist in compounds? (1) bonded by a triple covalent bond (2) as part of a cation (3) having lost 3 electrons to form an anion

a03.option_c: SiH₄ has a higher bp than CH₄.
a03.option_d: Water has a higher bp than CH₄.

a03.question: Which statement can be explained by hydrogen bonding?
a03.option_a: Ethanol has a higher bp than propane.
a03.option_b: HCl has a higher bp than SiH₄.
a03.option_d: Propanone has a higher bp than propane.

a03.question: Which features does Al₂Cl₆ have? (1) Each aluminium is surrounded by four chlorines. (2) There are twelve non-bonded electron pairs. (3) Each aluminium contributes electrons to four covalent bonds.
a03.explanation: There are 16 lone pairs; Al contributes to three bonds and accepts a dative bond.

a03.question: C₂O is C=C=O with no unpaired electrons. How many lone pairs does it have?
a03.explanation: Two on O and one on the terminal carbon.

a03.question: Which is the only gas at room temperature and pressure?

a03.question: P has hydrogen bonding; Q has van der Waals forces only (similar M_r). How does P compare? (1) more soluble in water (2) higher melting point (3) more viscous
a03.explanation: Hydrogen bonding strengthens the forces and allows bonding with water.

a03.question: Which elements can form π bonds with atoms of other elements? (1) oxygen (2) nitrogen (3) fluorine
In which fluoride is the F–X–F angle largest (X in Period 2)?

Why does iodine have instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces? (1) I₂ is polar and attracted to a lone pair on a neighbour. (2) I₂ has a fluctuating dipole because its electrons are more mobile than its nuclei. (3) The charge cloud may become unsymmetrical and attract other I₂ molecules.
Methylpropan-1-ol has a lower bp than butan-1-ol. Why?
a03.option_c: It has weaker van der Waals' forces.

a03.question: Which forces can exist between urea molecules? (1) hydrogen bonding (2) permanent dipole–dipole forces (3) instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces
a03.explanation: N–H and C=O groups; all molecules have temporary dipoles.

a03.question: Compared with HI, the bond in HBr has: (1) greater bond energy (2) smaller bond length (3) greater polarity
a03.explanation: Br is smaller and more electronegative.

a03.question: Which pair has species with different shapes?

a03.option_b: Al has an incomplete valence shell.
a03.option_c: The bonds around Al are planar.
a03.option_d: The molecules contain co-ordinate and covalent bonding.

a03.question: Which features are present in one N₂ molecule? (1) three π bonds (2) three shared pairs of electrons (3) two lone pairs of electrons
a03.explanation: N≡N is one σ and two π; one lone pair on each N.

a03.question: Which properties are due to hydrogen bonding between water molecules? (1) higher bp than H₂S (2) ice floats on water (3) H–O–H angle about 104°
a03.explanation: The angle is due to VSEPR.

a03.question: N₂ (bp 77 K) and CO (bp 82 K) both have M_r 28. What could explain the difference?
a03.option_b: N₂ has σ and π bonding, CO σ only.
a03.option_c: N₂ has a strong N≡N bond.

a03.question: Isomers of M_r 72 (pentane 36 °C, 2-methylbutane 28 °C, dimethylpropane 10 °C). Which explanation is correct?
a03.option_a: Boiling point depends on chain length only.
a03.option_b: More branching raises the boiling point.

a03.question: Which type of bonding is never found in elements?
