a11.question: Which statement about Group 17 redox chemistry is correct?
a11.option_a: Chlorine will oxidise bromide but not iodide.
a11.option_b: Fluorine is the weakest oxidising agent of F₂, Cl₂, Br₂, I₂.
a11.option_c: Iodide is the weakest reducing agent of the halides.
a11.option_d: When chlorine reacts with water, chlorine is both oxidised and reduced.

a11.question: A tube of HI and a tube of HBr are placed in an environment at temperature T. Which observations are possible? (1) A brown vapour appears in one tube and nothing in the other. (2) A brown vapour appears in one tube and a purple vapour in the other. (3) No change is seen in either tube.
a11.explanation: HI decomposes at a lower temperature than HBr, so brown Br₂ alone is not possible.

a11.question: NaI reacts with conc. H₂SO₄ to give NaHSO₄, H₂S, SO₂ and S. In the formation of which product has the oxidation state of sulfur changed by 8?
A tube of HBr(g) and a tube of HI(g) are heated to the same temperature. Which observations are possible?
a11.option_a: HBr: brown vapour; HI: no change
a11.option_b: HBr: purple vapour; HI: no change
a11.option_c: HBr: no change; HI: brown vapour
a11.option_d: HBr: no change; HI: purple vapour
a11.explanation: HI is less stable and forms purple I₂ first.

a11.question: 0.125 mol of Cl₂ reacts with excess cold aqueous NaOH. What mass of the sodium–oxygen–chlorine product is formed?
a11.explanation: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O; 0.125 mol NaClO × 74.5 = 9.31 g.

a11.question: Silver chloride dissolves in aqueous ammonia. What happens? (1) Ammonia forms a complex with the Ag⁺ ion. (2) Ammonia acts as a Brønsted–Lowry base. (3) A redox reaction occurs.
a11.explanation: NH₃ acts as a ligand (Lewis base).

a11.question: What are the oxidation numbers of chlorine in the products of Cl₂ with cold and with hot aqueous NaOH?
Under standard conditions, which statement is correct?
a11.explanation: Chlorine is the stronger oxidising agent.

a11.question: HI breaks down more quickly than HCl on heating. Which statements explain this? (1) The H–I bond is weaker than the H–Cl bond. (2) The breakdown of HI has a smaller activation energy than that of HCl. (3) The breakdown of HI is more exothermic than that of HCl.
a11.explanation: It is less endothermic, not exothermic.

a11.question: X gives a precipitate with aqueous AgNO₃ that remains undissolved with concentrated ammonia. What could X be? (1) iodomethane (2) 2-bromobutane (3) 2-chlorobutane
a11.explanation: Only AgI is insoluble in concentrated ammonia.

a11.question: Aqueous AgNO₃ gives a pale yellow precipitate with a sodium halide powder; concentrated ammonia dissolves part of it, leaving a darker yellow precipitate. What might the powder be?
Which reaction occurs when chlorine dissolves in water?
a11.explanation: Disproportionation to HCl and chloric(I) acid.

a11.question: Astatine is below iodine in Group 17. Which statement is most likely correct?
a11.option_a: AgAt dissolves in excess dilute ammonia.
a11.option_b: Astatine and KCl(aq) react to give KAt and chlorine.
a11.option_c: KAt(aq) and dilute H₂SO₄ give white fumes of HAt.
a11.option_d: NaAt(s) and concentrated H₂SO₄ react to form astatine.
a11.explanation: At⁻ is a strong reducing agent, so conc. H₂SO₄ oxidises it.

a11.question: A salt with two ions: acidified AgNO₃ gives a yellow precipitate; dilute H₂SO₄ gives a white precipitate. Which ions are in the filtrates P (from test 1) and Q (from test 2)?

Astatine is below iodine in Group 17. Which statements about At can be predicted? (1) At₂ reacts with hydrogen more slowly than I₂. (2) At⁻ ions react with I₂(aq) to form At₂. (3) At₂ is a dark coloured solid at room temperature.
a11.explanation: Reactivity and oxidising power fall down the group.

a11.question: Astatine is below iodine in Group 17. Which statements are likely to be correct? (1) It is a dark-coloured solid. (2) It is a more powerful oxidising agent than iodine. (3) Its hydride is thermally stable.
Which statement about bromine is correct?
a11.option_a: Bromine is insoluble in non-polar solvents.
a11.option_b: Bromine vapour is more dense than air.
a11.option_c: Bromine does not vaporise significantly under normal conditions.

a11.question: Aqueous AgNO₃ and aqueous BaCl₂ give a white precipitate that dissolves in excess dilute ammonia. Excess dilute HNO₃ is added to the colourless solution. What is the white precipitate Z?
a11.explanation: HNO₃ destroys the complex, reforming AgCl.

a11.question: NaCl with conc. H₂SO₄ gives a colourless acidic gas; NaI gives purple vapour; with conc. H₃PO₄ both give a colourless acidic gas. Which deduction is correct?
a11.option_a: H₃PO₄ is a stronger oxidising agent than H₂SO₄.
a11.option_b: H₃PO₄ is a stronger oxidising agent than iodine.
a11.option_c: H₂SO₄ is a stronger oxidising agent than chlorine.
a11.option_d: H₂SO₄ is a stronger oxidising agent than iodine.
a11.explanation: H₂SO₄ oxidises I⁻ to I₂ but not Cl⁻.

a11.question: A white powder (NaCl and NaI) is dissolved in water and excess AgNO₃ is added to form precipitate X. Excess concentrated ammonia is then added to leave precipitate Y. Which statement is correct?
a11.option_a: X is a pure white colour.

a11.question: X is an organic compound that gives a precipitate with AgNO₃. Some or all of it remains with excess dilute ammonia. What could X be? (1) 2-chlorobutane (2) 2-bromobutane (3) iodomethane
a11.explanation: AgCl dissolves in dilute ammonia; AgBr only partially.

a11.question: NaCl and NaI both react with conc. H₂SO₄ at room temperature. NaCl gives NaHSO₄ and HCl; NaI also gives HI, I₂, SO₂, S and H₂S. What explains this?
a11.option_b: HCl is more volatile than HI.
a11.option_c: Iodide ions are better reducing agents than chloride ions.
a11.option_d: H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent with NaI.

a11.question: An excess of Cl₂ is passed through 60 cm^3 of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ cold NaOH, and in a separate experiment through the same hot NaOH. How much more NaCl forms with hot NaOH?
a11.explanation: n(NaOH) = 0.006 mol: cold gives 0.003 mol NaCl; hot gives 0.005 mol.

a11.question: Fluorine and iodine have different melting points due to van der Waals' forces. Which row is correct?
a11.option_a: m.p. F₂ > I₂; vdW F₂ > I₂
a11.option_b: m.p. F₂ > I₂; vdW F₂ < I₂
a11.option_c: m.p. F₂ < I₂; vdW F₂ < I₂
a11.option_d: m.p. F₂ < I₂; vdW F₂ > I₂

a11.question: Aqueous Cl₂, Br₂ and I₂ are each added to NaCl, NaBr and NaI solutions (nine experiments) and shaken with hexane. How many tubes contain a purple upper layer?
a11.explanation: Purple iodine is present in Cl₂/NaI, Br₂/NaI, and in all three I₂ experiments.

a11.question: Which chlorine species in water is responsible for killing bacteria?
a11.option_d: Cl₂ only as an unreacted gas
a11.explanation: ClO⁻ and HClO kill bacteria by oxidation.

a11.question: HCl and HI have different thermal stabilities. Which row identifies the more stable compound and the correct reason?
a11.option_a: HCl; the Cl–Cl bond is stronger than I–I
a11.option_b: HCl; the H–Cl bond is stronger than H–I
a11.option_c: HI; the Cl–Cl bond is stronger than I–I
a11.option_d: HI; the H–Cl bond is stronger than H–I
a11.explanation: The H–X bond is stronger when X is smaller.

a11.question: Unreacted AgBr is removed from photographic film with sodium thiosulfate. What is the function of the thiosulfate ion?
a11.option_a: to make the silver ions soluble

a11.question: Chlorine atoms in the upper atmosphere break down ozone. Which statements are correct? (1) The chlorine atoms act as catalysts. (2) The chlorine atoms are free radicals. (3) The chlorine atoms are formed by heterolytic fission of a covalent bond in CFCs.
Conc. H₂SO₄ reacts with NaI to give S, I₂, H₂S and SO₂. Which statement is correct?
a11.option_a: Hydrogen sulfide is the product of a reduction reaction.
a11.option_b: Iodide ions are stronger oxidising agents than sulfate ions.
a11.option_c: Sulfur atoms are both oxidised and reduced.
a11.option_d: Sulfur atoms are oxidised to make sulfur dioxide.

a11.question: NaOH reacts with 3 mol of chlorine to give 5 mol of NaCl and 1 mol of X, the only other chlorine product. What is X?
Which statement about Group 17 redox chemistry is correct?
a11.option_a: Br⁻ will reduce Cl₂ but not I₂.
a11.option_b: Cl₂ will oxidise Br⁻ but not I⁻.
a11.option_c: F₂ is the weakest oxidising agent.
a11.option_d: I⁻ is the weakest reducing agent.
a11.explanation: I₂ is a weaker oxidising agent than Br₂.

a11.question: Element X reacts with cold dilute aqueous NaOH to form two chlorine-containing products. What are their oxidation states?
Chlorine is added to cold aqueous NaOH and in a separate experiment to hot NaOH. Which oxidation states of chlorine are found in all reactants and products?
71.0 g of chlorine reacts with excess NaOH at a particular temperature and gives exactly 35.5 g of product X. What is X?
a11.explanation: 1 mol Cl₂ gives 1/3 mol NaClO₃ = 35.5 g (hot NaOH).

a11.question: Compound Q is a white soluble solid. Concentrated H₂SO₄ gives steamy white fumes which form a white precipitate with AgNO₃ that dissolves in dilute ammonia. What is Q?
How do the covalent bond strength and the van der Waals' forces change from Cl₂ to Br₂ to I₂?
Sodium bromide reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid. What is observed?
The volatility of the Group 17 elements decreases down the group. What is responsible?
a11.option_d: number of electrons in the molecule
a11.explanation: More electrons give stronger instantaneous dipole forces.

a11.question: Br₂ + SO₂ + 2H₂O → 2HBr + H₂SO₄; 2HBr + Cl₂ → Br₂ + 2HCl. Which is the order from strongest to weakest oxidising agent?
a11.explanation: Cl₂ oxidises Br⁻; Br₂ oxidises SO₂.

a11.question: Chlorine reacts with hot aqueous NaOH. Which oxidation states does chlorine show in the products? (1) −1 (2) +3 (3) +1
Which explains the decrease in volatility down Group 17?
a11.option_a: Instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces get stronger.

a11.question: Conc. H₂SO₄ with NaCl gives HCl, and with NaI gives I₂. Which statement explains this?
a11.option_a: H₂SO₄ is an oxidising agent and chloride ions are more easily oxidised.
a11.option_b: H₂SO₄ is an oxidising agent and iodide ions are more easily oxidised.
a11.option_c: H₂SO₄ is a reducing agent and chloride ions are more easily reduced.
a11.option_d: H₂SO₄ is a reducing agent and iodide ions are more easily reduced.
a11.explanation: I⁻ is the stronger reducing agent.

a11.question: Gases from heating Ca(OH)₂ and NH₄Cl pass over solid CaO, which absorbs water and a gas, W. W is oxidised by Cl₂ to X (an element) and Y (acidic). Y reacts with W to give Z. What are X and Z?
a11.explanation: W = NH₃; Y = HCl; Z = NH₄Cl.

a11.question: How do the volatility and the oxidising ability of the halogens change from chlorine to iodine?
Reaction 1: chlorine + cold aqueous NaOH gives solution Z. Reaction 2: Z is heated and forms ClO₃⁻ and Cl⁻. Which equations represent 1 and 2?
a11.option_c: 1: Cl₂ + 2OH⁻ → ClO⁻ + Cl⁻ + H₂O; 2: 2ClO⁻ + 2OH⁻ → ClO₃⁻ + Cl⁻ + H₂O
a11.explanation: Cl₂ + 2OH⁻ gives ClO⁻, which disproportionates on heating.

a11.question: Which statement about the halogens is correct?
a11.option_a: Iodine cannot behave as an oxidising agent.
a11.option_b: Volatility increases from chlorine to iodine because of increasing size.
a11.option_c: When equimolar chlorine and hydrogen are exploded, only one product forms.
a11.option_d: Conc. H₂SO₄ with NaBr gives H₂S.

a11.question: Cold NaOH forms sodium chlorate(X) and hot NaOH forms sodium chlorate(Y). Which equation is correct?
A white compound G gives a precipitate with AgNO₃ that does not dissolve in ammonia, and warming it with concentrated H₂SO₄ gives a gas mixture including H₂S. What is G?
a11.explanation: AgI is insoluble in ammonia; I⁻ reduces H₂SO₄ to H₂S.

a11.question: Under standard conditions, which statement is correct?
a11.explanation: Cl₂ is the stronger oxidising agent.

a11.question: Conc. H₂SO₄ is added to NaCl, NaBr and NaI separately. With which does the acid act as an oxidising agent?
a11.explanation: Br⁻ and I⁻ reduce the sulfuric acid.

a11.question: Bromine reacts with warm NaOH(aq) like chlorine with hot NaOH. 30.2 g of a Na–Br–O product forms. What mass of NaOH has reacted?
a11.explanation: NaBrO₃ (150.9) = 0.200 mol; 3Br₂ + 6NaOH → 5NaBr + NaBrO₃ + 3H₂O needs 1.20 mol NaOH.

a11.question: Hot concentrated H₂SO₄ is added to KX. Which halides give a mixture of products including a halogen X₂? (1) potassium iodide (2) potassium bromide (3) potassium chloride
Which statements about sodium chloride are correct? (1) It is a product of Cl₂ with cold aqueous NaOH. (2) It is a product of Cl₂ with hot aqueous NaOH. (3) It is a product of Cl₂ with aqueous NaBr.
Chlorine and bromine have different volatilities. Which is more volatile and why?
a11.option_c: chlorine; instantaneous dipole forces greater in bromine
a11.option_d: chlorine; instantaneous dipole forces greater in chlorine

a11.question: Which property is smaller for chlorine than for bromine?
a11.option_c: solubility of the silver halide in NH₃(aq)
a11.option_d: strength of van der Waals' forces between molecules

a11.question: 6NaOH + 3Cl₂ → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O. Which statement is correct?
a11.option_a: The oxidation numbers of Cl and H both change.
a11.option_b: The oxidation numbers of Cl in the products are −1 and +1.
a11.option_c: If the NaOH is cold the reaction gives NaClO instead of NaClO₃.

a11.question: Which explains why iodine is less volatile than chlorine?
a11.option_a: Chlorine is more electronegative so has more repulsion.
a11.option_b: More electrons in iodine give larger instantaneous dipole forces.
a11.explanation: The I₂ molecules have more electrons.

a11.question: Which property explains the trend in volatility of the elements down Group 17?
Which element is the strongest oxidising agent? (A: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^5; B: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2; C: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^4; D: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2)
Which statement about Group 17 elements and compounds is correct?
a11.option_a: Cl₂ with cold concentrated NaOH gives NaCl and NaClO₃.
a11.option_b: HCl is more stable than HBr because Cl is less electronegative.
a11.option_c: Iodide ions are oxidised to iodine by concentrated sulfuric acid.
a11.option_d: AgI is soluble in dilute aqueous ammonia.

a11.question: Which substance, warmed with aqueous NH₄Cl, would produce an alkaline gas?
a11.explanation: The ethoxide ion is a strong base that deprotonates NH₄⁺ to give NH₃.

a11.question: Chlorine reacts with aqueous NaOH: Cl goes 0 → −1 and 0 → +1. What are the conditions and the colour of the silver salt containing chlorine in oxidation state −1?
CH₃NH₂ reacts with HCl to give CH₃NH₃⁺Cl⁻. The salt is heated with aqueous NaOH. What are the products?
5 cm^3 of 0.05 mol dm⁻³ NaCl is mixed with 5 cm^3 of 0.05 mol dm⁻³ KI; 10 cm^3 of 0.05 mol dm⁻³ acidified AgNO₃ is added, followed by an excess of concentrated ammonia. What is seen?
Which mixtures both result in oxidation of a halide ion?
a11.explanation: I⁻ is oxidised by Br₂; Br⁻ is oxidised by sulfuric acid.

a11.question: Which statement is correct when descending Group 17 from chlorine to iodine?
a11.option_a: The hydrides become less stable as they become weaker reducing agents.
a11.option_b: The hydrides become more stable as the elements become less reactive.
a11.option_c: Volatility decreases as van der Waals' forces increase.
a11.option_d: Volatility increases as the size of the molecules increases.

a11.question: Which reagents produce a solution of sodium chlorate(V)? (1) chlorine and hot concentrated NaOH (2) chlorine and cold dilute NaOH (3) chlorine dissolved in water at room temperature
Z is a compound of sodium, chlorine and oxygen with 45.1% oxygen. It is prepared by reacting NaOH with chlorine. What are the conditions and the oxidation state of chlorine in Z?

Which statements about ammonium chloride are correct? (1) It reacts with hot aqueous NaOH to produce an alkaline gas. (2) In solution, it reacts with AgNO₃ to give a white precipitate. (3) When solid, it reacts with conc. H₂SO₄ to produce chlorine.
Which statement relating to Group 17 and their compounds is correct?
a11.option_a: Bromine reduces KI to form iodine.
a11.option_b: Iodide gives a white precipitate with AgNO₃.
a11.option_c: Bromide gives a white precipitate with AgNO₃.
a11.option_d: Chlorine reacts with hydrogen to form a colourless gas.

a11.question: An excess of chlorine is bubbled into 100 cm^3 of hot 6.0 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. How many moles of NaCl are produced?
Which statement is correct for the element in Period 3, Group 13?
a11.option_a: It has the highest melting point in its period.
a11.option_b: It has exactly one electron in n = 3.
a11.option_c: It forms an oxide that reacts with aqueous NaOH.
a11.option_d: It forms a chloride that gives a neutral solution.

a11.question: X₂ has weaker covalent bonds than Y₂; X₂ has stronger instantaneous dipole forces than Z₂; Y₂ is a stronger oxidising agent than Z₂. What could X, Y, Z be?
a11.explanation: I₂ has weaker bonds than Cl₂ and stronger forces than Br₂; Cl₂ is a stronger oxidant than Br₂.

a11.question: Chlorine reacts with aqueous NaOH forming two chlorine-containing products. Which row is correct?
Chlorine is bubbled through aqueous NaI with a layer of hexane. What is observed in the lower and upper layers?
a11.option_a: lower colourless becomes brown; upper colourless becomes coloured
a11.option_b: lower colourless becomes brown; upper unchanged
a11.option_c: lower brown becomes colourless; upper becomes coloured
a11.option_d: lower brown becomes colourless; upper unchanged
a11.explanation: I₂ is formed and dissolves into the hexane.

a11.question: Which statement is correct?
a11.option_a: NaCl produces chlorine with conc. H₂SO₄.
a11.option_c: NaBr produces bromine with conc. H₂SO₄.
a11.option_d: NaBr produces bromine with iodine in aqueous KI.

a11.question: W, X contain 25 cm^3 of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ BaCl₂ and MgCl₂ respectively with 25 cm^3 of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaOH added; Y, Z contain BaCl₂ and MgCl₂ with 25 cm^3 of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄. Which has the higher pH (W or X) and the greater mass of precipitate (Y or Z)?
a11.explanation: Mg(OH)₂ precipitates in X, lowering the pH. BaSO₄ precipitates in Y; MgSO₄ is soluble.

a11.question: What is the oxidation state of the chlorine-containing species that kills bacteria in drinking water?

P is a mixture of two of AgCl, AgBr and AgI. It is shaken with dilute ammonia leaving a yellow solid Q; the filtrate gives a white precipitate R with nitric acid. Q and R are warmed with conc. H₂SO₄. What is observed?
a11.option_a: Q: violet fumes; R: orange fumes
a11.option_b: Q: violet fumes; R: steamy fumes
a11.option_c: Q: steamy fumes; R: violet fumes
a11.option_d: Q: orange fumes; R: steamy fumes
a11.explanation: Q is AgI (violet iodine); R is AgCl (steamy HCl).

a11.question: When conc. H₂SO₄ is added to NaBr, Br₂ forms among other products, but NaCl gives only HCl and NaHSO₄. What is the reason?
a11.option_a: Bromine is less volatile than chlorine.
a11.option_b: Hydrochloric acid is a weak acid.
a11.option_c: Sulfuric acid is not an oxidising agent.
a11.option_d: The bromide ion is a stronger reducing agent than the chloride ion.

a11.question: Which statement about halogens or halide ions is correct?
a11.option_a: Bromide gives a white precipitate with AgNO₃.
a11.option_b: Bromine does not oxidise chloride ions.
a11.option_c: Fluorine atoms form cations by accepting electrons.
a11.option_d: Chloride is a stronger reducing agent than iodide.
a11.explanation: Br₂ is a weaker oxidant than Cl₂.

a11.question: Iodine has a higher melting point than chlorine. What is the reason?
Two salts, NaI and NaCl, are added separately to warm conc. H₂SO₄; aqueous solutions are added to AgNO₃ and then concentrated NH₃(aq). Which row is correct?
a11.explanation: I⁻ reduces sulfuric acid to H₂S; AgI is insoluble in ammonia.

a11.question: Which statement about these equations is correct? (1) 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂; (2) 4KClO₃ → 3KClO₄ + KCl; (3) 6KOH + 3Cl₂ → 3H₂O + 5KCl + KClO₃
a11.option_a: Equation 1 forms a compound that kills bacteria in drinking water.
a11.explanation: Chlorine is both oxidised and reduced in each.

a11.question: A solid sodium halide NaX is reacted with conc. H₂SO₄; the lowest oxidation state of sulfur in the products is +4. Halogen Y₂ is less volatile than X₂. What are NaX and Y₂?
a11.explanation: NaBr gives SO₂ (+4); iodine is less volatile than bromine.

a11.question: Compound Q dissolves in water; Q(aq) does not react with dilute H₂SO₄ and gives a precipitate with AgNO₃ that is partially soluble in ammonia. What could Q be?
a11.explanation: No Ba²⁺ (no BaSO₄) and AgBr is partially soluble.

a11.question: Chlorine is reacted with cold aqueous NaOH. Which statement is correct?
a11.option_a: Chlorine is both oxidised and reduced.
a11.option_b: Chlorine is neither oxidised nor reduced.
a11.option_c: Chlorine is oxidised but not reduced.
a11.option_d: Chlorine is reduced but not oxidised.

a11.question: Sodium is added to water to form solution Y. When powdered X is added, the pH falls. Which two compounds could each be X?
a11.explanation: Mg²⁺ precipitates Mg(OH)₂ and Al(OH)₃ reacts with OH⁻.

a11.question: Which row shows a correct statement and a correct explanation?
a11.option_a: iodine is a solid because the I–I bond strength is high
a11.option_b: HI decomposition is more endothermic than HCl because Cl is more reactive
a11.option_c: Cl₂ in aqueous KI gives a purple solution because Cl₂ is a stronger oxidant than I₂
a11.option_d: conc. H₂SO₄ on KI gives purple vapour because I⁻ is oxidised by the acid
a11.explanation: I₂ vapour forms as I⁻ is oxidised to I₂.

a11.question: Which statement is correct?
a11.option_a: HBr reduces concentrated H₂SO₄ to form SO₂ gas.
a11.option_b: HBr decomposes at a higher temperature than HCl.
a11.option_c: HBr shaken with aqueous AgNO₃ gives a yellow precipitate.
a11.option_d: HBr bubbled through aqueous iodine makes it colourless.
a11.explanation: Br⁻ is oxidised to Br₂ as H₂SO₄ is reduced.

a11.question: ICl is made from Cl₂ and I₂. 5ICl + 3H₂O → 5HCl + HIO₃ + 2I₂. Which row is correct?
a11.option_a: oxidation number of I in ICl is +1; I is oxidised to I₂
a11.option_b: oxidation number of I in ICl is +1; I is oxidised to form HIO₃
a11.option_c: oxidation number of I in ICl is −1; Cl is reduced
a11.option_d: oxidation number of I in ICl is −1; I is oxidised to HIO₃

a11.question: NH₄Cl reacts with NaOH in aqueous solution. Which statement is correct?
a11.option_a: The reaction gives rise to two different polar product molecules.
a11.option_b: The bond angle in the nitrogen-containing species remains unchanged.
a11.option_c: The ammonium ion acts as a base.
a11.option_d: The oxidation state of nitrogen increases.
a11.explanation: NH₃ and H₂O are both polar.

a12.question: Which statements explain why sulfur dioxide is used as a food preservative? (1) It is a reducing agent and therefore an anti-oxidant. (2) It prevents alcohols in foods forming sour-tasting acids. (3) It does not smell and therefore can be used in large quantities.
a12.explanation: SO₂ has a pungent smell. It stops oxidation of ethanol to ethanoic acid.

a12.question: Sulfur dioxide is removed from furnace gases by reacting it with calcium hydroxide. What is the main product formed initially?

Element X is a solid found in some fuels. Its oxide Y is formed in car engines and is acidic; Y is further oxidised to Z in the atmosphere. Which statements are correct? (1) Molecule Y has lone pairs of electrons. (2) The atmospheric oxidation of Y to Z is a catalysed reaction. (3) Y is a colourless gas.
a12.explanation: X = S, Y = SO₂ and Z = SO₃; NO₂ catalyses SO₂ → SO₃.

a12.question: Mohr's salt contains Fe²⁺, SO₄²⁻ and a second cation. Heating with NaOH(aq) gives a colourless gas that dissolves in water to give an alkaline solution, and a green precipitate. What are the gas and the precipitate?
a12.explanation: NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ → NH₃ + H₂O; Fe²⁺ + 2OH⁻ → green Fe(OH)₂.

a12.question: Which statement about the ammonium ion is correct?
a12.option_b: It forms when ammonia behaves as an acid.
a12.option_c: It is unreactive when heated with NaOH(aq).
a12.option_d: The bonds are all the same length.
a12.explanation: NH₄⁺ is a regular tetrahedron (109.5°) formed when NH₃ acts as a base.

a12.question: CO, NO₂ and SO₂ are atmospheric pollutants. Which reaction occurs in the atmosphere?
a12.option_a: CO is spontaneously oxidised to CO₂.
a12.option_b: NO₂ is reduced to NO by CO.
a12.option_c: NO₂ is reduced to NO by SO₂.
a12.option_d: SO₂ is oxidised to SO₃ by CO₂.

a12.question: Under atmospheric conditions, in which transformations is sulfur dioxide a reagent or catalyst? (1) NO₂ to NO (2) NO to NO₂ (3) CO to CO₂

Element X (carbon, nitrogen or sulfur) forms a pollutant oxide Y that is further oxidised to Z. Student P: "Y has lone pairs." Student Q: "The oxidation number of X increases by 1 from Y to Z." Who is correct?
a12.explanation: CO, NO and SO₂ have lone pairs, and the oxidation number rises by 2 in each case.

a12.question: Which statements about SO₂ as a food preservative are correct? (1) SO₂ behaves as an antioxidant. (2) Aqueous SO₂ contains SO₃²⁻ ions. (3) SO₂ inhibits the growth of mould and yeasts.
a12.explanation: SO₂ is a reducing agent and an anti-microbial.

a12.question: 4.70 g of an ammonium salt is heated with excess aqueous NaOH and 1.41 dm^3 of NH₃ are produced (room conditions). Which salt was used?
Which descriptions of the ammonium ion are correct? (1) It contains ten electrons. (2) It has a bond angle of 109.5°. (3) It has only three bonding pairs of electrons.
Which statement about ammonia and/or the ammonium ion is correct?
a12.option_a: Ammonia is basic because it can donate H⁺.
a12.option_b: Ammonium ions are basic because they can accept H⁺.
a12.option_c: Heating ammonium ions with NaOH(aq) gives ammonia.
a12.option_d: The H–N–H angle in NH₄⁺ is 2.5° less than in NH₃.

a12.question: Which reaction does not contribute to acid rain?
a12.option_c: NO + CO in a catalytic converter

a12.question: NH₃ and H₂S form (NH₄)₂S, which dissolves in water. NaOH(aq) added to one portion gives gas X; HCl(aq) added to another gives gas Y. What are X and Y?
a12.explanation: Alkali releases NH₃; acid releases H₂S.

a12.question: What happens to NO, NO₂, CO and hydrocarbons in a catalytic converter?
a12.option_a: NO oxidised; NO₂ oxidised; CO reduced; hydrocarbons oxidised
a12.option_c: NO reduced; NO₂ reduced; CO oxidised; hydrocarbons oxidised
a12.explanation: Nitrogen oxides are reduced; CO and hydrocarbons are oxidised.

a12.question: Which is not an effect of acid rain?

Which statements about ammonia are correct? (1) An ammonia molecule has three bond pairs and one lone pair. (2) When ammonia is bubbled into water the pH increases. (3) Ammonia can be made by warming ammonium sulfate with aqueous hydrochloric acid.
a12.explanation: A strong alkali (NaOH) is needed to release ammonia.

a12.question: Ammonium sulfate and ammonium nitrate are fertilisers with the same effect on soil pH. Which has the higher % N by mass and what is the effect on pH?
a12.explanation: NH₄NO₃ is 35% N vs 21%. Ammonium salts acidify soil.

a12.question: What problems might result from excess nitrogen fertiliser applied to paddy fields with fish pens? (1) decreased fish production (2) decreased levels of oxygen in the water (3) increased growth of algae

X is nitrogen or sulfur and forms pollutant oxide Y; 1 mol of Y reacts with 0.5 mol O₂ to give Z. Which statements can be correct? (1) The oxidation number of X increases by two from Y to Z. (2) Y has an unpaired electron in its molecule. (3) Y is a non-polar molecule.
a12.explanation: NO + ½O₂ → NO₂ (NO has an unpaired electron); both NO and SO₂ are polar.

a12.question: NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺. Which statement is correct?
a12.option_a: The ammonia molecule contains a dative covalent bond.
a12.option_b: The ammonium ion is a Brønsted–Lowry base.
a12.option_c: The H–N–H angle changes from 107° to 90°.
a12.option_d: The number of electrons surrounding each nitrogen atom does not change.
a12.explanation: Eight electrons surround N in both species.

a12.question: Which statements about acid rain are correct? (1) It forms when oxides of nitrogen or sulfur react with water in the atmosphere. (2) It increases the concentration of heavy metal ions in water courses. (3) Nitrogen dioxide catalyses the formation of SO₃ from SO₂.
Which nitrogen-containing species are present in an aqueous solution of ammonia?
a12.option_a: ammonia molecules and amide ions only
a12.option_b: ammonia molecules and ammonium ions only

a12.question: 60 g of nitrogen monoxide reacts with an excess of carbon monoxide in a catalytic converter. What is produced?
a12.explanation: 2NO + 2CO → N₂ + 2CO₂: 2 mol NO gives 1 mol N₂ (28 g) and 2 mol CO₂ (88 g).

a12.question: What might result from release of SO₂ into the atmosphere? (1) reduction of NO₂ to NO (2) depletion of aquatic life (3) corrosion of limestone statues
Which fertiliser contains the greatest percentage of nitrogen by mass?

Which statements explain why nitrogen gas is unreactive? (1) Nitrogen atoms are highly electronegative. (2) Nitrogen molecules are non-polar. (3) The triple bond between nitrogen atoms is very strong.
a12.explanation: Electronegativity is not the reason; non-polar N₂ does not attract polar reagents and the N≡N bond (944 kJ mol⁻¹) is very strong.

a12.question: Why do the reactions of nitrogen and oxygen need such high temperatures?
a12.option_a: lack of reactivity of nitrogen due to a half-filled 2p subshell
a12.option_b: lack of reactivity of nitrogen due to the strength of the N₂ bond
a12.option_c: lack of reactivity of oxygen due to electron repulsion in a 2p orbital
a12.option_d: lack of reactivity of oxygen due to the strength of the O₂ bond

a12.question: Which statements about catalytic converters are correct? (1) CO is oxidised to CO₂. (2) They have a very large surface area. (3) NO₂ is reduced to NO.

In which different forms does nitrogen exist in compounds? (1) bonded by a triple covalent bond (2) as part of a cation (3) in an oxidation state of +5
Which row gives a natural and a man-made source of nitrogen oxides?
a12.option_b: electrical discharges; by-product of the Haber process
a12.option_c: decomposition of plants; internal combustion engines

a12.question: Which statements describe an oxide of nitrogen acting as a pollutant? (1) NO reacts with oxygen to form NO₂, which contributes to acid rain. Why does Mg(OH)₂ dissolve in aqueous NH₄Cl but not in aqueous NaCl?
a12.option_a: The NH₄⁺ ionic radius is similar to Mg²⁺.
a12.option_c: Na⁺ and Mg²⁺ have the same number of electrons.
a12.option_d: The NH₄⁺ ion can donate a proton.

a12.question: Ammonium cyanate, heated in the absence of air, gives only urea, CO(NH₂)₂. What is the formula of the cyanate ion?
a12.explanation: NH₄OCN is an isomer of urea.

a12.question: Which statement about nitrogen compounds NH₃, NH₂NH₂ and N₂ is correct?
a12.option_a: The N–N bond in NH₂NH₂ is polar.
a12.option_b: NH₃ and NH₂NH₂ have lone pairs but N₂ does not.
a12.option_c: The oxidation number of each N in NH₂NH₂ is +2.
a12.option_d: The reaction of nitrogen with hydrogen has a high activation energy.
a12.explanation: N≡N is very strong. The N–N bond in hydrazine is non-polar; N is −2 in NH₂NH₂; N₂ has lone pairs too.

a12.question: Which statements about ceramics are correct? (1) Ceramics are good electrical conductors. (2) Ceramics are strong materials. (3) Ceramics have high melting points.
Which statement is correct?
a12.option_a: Ammonia reacts with alkalis to form the ammonium ion.
a12.option_b: Ammonium chloride contains ionic, covalent and co-ordinate bonds.
a12.option_c: The ammonium ion reacts with acids to produce ammonia.
a12.option_d: The bond angle in the ammonium ion is about 107°.
a12.explanation: NH₄⁺ and Cl⁻ are ionic; N–H are covalent with one dative.

a12.question: 5.6 g of CO reacts with an excess of NO in a catalytic converter. What is produced?
a12.explanation: 0.2 mol CO + 0.2 mol NO → 0.2 mol CO₂ + 0.1 mol N₂.

a12.question: Which gases dissolve in water causing a lowering of the pH? (1) ammonia (2) sulfur dioxide (3) nitrogen dioxide
Sodium azide is dissolved in water; acidified AgNO₃ gives a white precipitate; aqueous ammonia is then added. The azide ion N₃⁻ behaves like Cl⁻. What can be predicted?
a12.explanation: Like AgCl, AgN₃ dissolves in NH₃(aq).

a12.question: Which type of reaction occurs when solid ammonium sulfate is heated with excess NaOH solution?
Which gas causes acid rain and is removed from car exhaust by a catalytic converter?

(2) The triple bond is not polar but the bonds in O₂ and Cl₂ are polar. (3) N atoms in N₂ have a full outer shell but those in O₂ and Cl₂ do not.
a12.explanation: O₂ and Cl₂ are also non-polar and all have octets.

a12.question: NH₃, CO₂ and H₂O react together to form ammonium carbonate. Which statement is correct?

a12.option_c: Nitrogen monoxide will react with carbon monoxide under suitable conditions.
a12.option_d: The formula of ammonium sulfate is NH₄SO₄.

a12.question: 6.90 g of an ammonium salt with excess NaOH(aq) gives 2.51 dm^3 of NH₃ (room conditions). Which salt?
a12.explanation: n(NH₃) = 0.105 mol; a 2:1 salt has 0.0523 mol so M_r = 132.

a12.question: Which pollutants react with oxygen on the surface of a catalytic converter? (1) NO₂ (2) unburnt fuel (3) CO
Which three gases are removed by a catalytic converter?
a12.explanation: It does not remove CO₂ or SO₂.

a12.question: Which statement about NH₃ + HCl → NH₄Cl is correct?
a12.option_b: The hydrogen atom from HCl donates a lone pair to nitrogen.
a12.option_c: The H–N–H angle is the same in NH₃ and NH₄⁺.
a12.option_d: The H–N–H angle in NH₄⁺ is the same as the H–C–H angle in methane.

a12.question: SO₂ reacts with calcium hydroxide in aqueous solution. What is the main product first formed?
a12.explanation: Acidic oxide + alkali gives a sulfite.

a12.question: What is the purpose of the heat exchanger in the Haber process?
a12.option_a: to cool the incoming gas to avoid overheating the catalyst
a12.option_b: to cool the products and separate NH₃
a12.option_c: to warm the incoming gas and shift the equilibrium to give more NH₃
a12.option_d: to warm the incoming gas and speed up the reaction
a12.explanation: Heat from the hot products warms the incoming gases.
